newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares drop after lower foreign purchases.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares drop after lower foreign purchases.

text.p: Jordan's stock market fell on Monday after a foreign fund buying spree behind a two week long surge in prices eased, dealers said.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.82 points to 163.00 points in turnover of 3.8 million dinars ($5.4 million), still dominated by emerging fund buying on a handful of mining and bank stock.
Jordan Cement, which has been riding the wave of the bull market, shed 0.22 dinars to close at 4.19 dinars. But it still dominated trade with over 1.4 million dinars in turnover.
The two mining stocks which have also been focus of interest, Jordan Phosphate Mines and Arab Potash, fell 0.08 dinars to 4.00 dinars and 0.05 dinars to 7.00 dinars respectively.
"The extent of foreign buying dropped on some of the stock which resulted in a retreat," said broker Husam al-Hanbali.
Brokers said local funds began selling as worries grew that foreign demand would drop further in the coming few days.
In banks, Jordan National Bank saw the heaviest buying orders which helped it rise 0.02 dinar to 2.29 dinars in trade worth around one million dinars.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 30 to eight while another ten traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.67 percent to 81.60 points, 2.15 percent down from the start of the year.
